What Is TDEE?

TDEE, or Total Daily Energy Expenditure, is the approximate number of calories your body burns in a full day. It combines the energy your body uses just to stay alive with the extra calories burned through movement, exercise, and daily activity. Knowing your TDEE gives you a starting point for setting calorie goals, whether you want to maintain, lose, or gain weight.

How Is TDEE Calculated?

TDEE is built from two pieces: your Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR) and your activity level.

Basal Metabolic Rate

BMR is the number of calories your body needs at complete rest to keep basic functions running, such as breathing and circulation.

Physical Activity and the Activity Multiplier

Everything beyond rest — walking, exercise, work, daily movement — adds to your calorie needs. This calculator applies an activity multiplier to your BMR based on how active you are.

The Mifflin-St Jeor Formula

This calculator uses the Mifflin-St Jeor equation, one of the most widely used formulas for estimating BMR from age, gender, height, and weight, then multiplies the result by your activity factor to estimate TDEE.

TDEE vs BMR

BMR represents the calories your body burns at rest. TDEE builds on that number by adding the calories burned through daily activity and exercise. In short, BMR is your baseline, and TDEE is your full-day total.

How to Use Your TDEE

For Weight Maintenance

Eating approximately around your TDEE may help maintain your current body weight over time.

For Weight Loss

A moderate calorie deficit below your TDEE may support gradual weight loss.

For Weight Gain

A controlled calorie surplus above your TDEE may support weight gain.

Activity Level Guide

LevelDescription
SedentaryLittle or no exercise
Lightly ActiveExercise 1–3 days per week
Moderately ActiveExercise 3–5 days per week
Very ActiveExercise 6–7 days per week
Extra ActiveVery intense exercise or physical job
